newsitem.title: USA: ADP says it sees double-digit revs growth.
newsitem.headline: ADP says it sees double-digit revs growth.

text.p: Automatic Data Processing Inc said it expects double digit revenue growth for the 1997 fiscal year ending in June, and sees consolidated margins improving in the second half of fiscal 1997.

In a statement, Arthur Weinbach, president and chief executive, said, "...We expect consolidated margins to improve in the second half of fiscal 1997. For the full fiscal year we continue to expect double-digit revenue growth and about 15 percent growth in earnings per share."

He noted that he saw a slowdown in revenue growth in the second half of the year because the company will have past the anniversary date of the acquisition of Paris-based GSI. ADP bought GSI in the fall of 1995.
